sections.title: Website development with React and Next.js
sections.text: We build website front ends with React and Next.js, the framework built on top of it. We choose the right rendering method for each page and connect it to your systems and data sources, on an architecture built to scale.

items.heading: Routing layer
items.label: Routes, pages and the rendering method for each

items.heading: Sources layer
items.label: CMS, internal systems and external services

sections.label: Requests travel down the stack, then come back rendered

sections.title: When a custom front end beats ready-made platforms

items.heading: Interactive interfaces
items.label: Calculators, dashboards, complex filters and experiences that depend on user state.

items.heading: Multiple integrations
items.label: Bringing internal systems or external services together in one interface.

items.heading: Large data volumes
items.label: Thousands of pages or records that need performance and control over rendering.

items.heading: Digital products
items.label: A web app with users, accounts and permissions.

items.heading: Multiple front ends
items.label: A website, an app and an admin dashboard on the same data source.

items.heading: Critical performance
items.label: Pages that must load fast under heavy load.

sections.title: We choose rendering to fit each page
sections.text: Not every page needs the same treatment. Next.js lets us choose how each page is rendered: content pages are pre-generated so they load fast and are read reliably, while pages that depend on user data are rendered on request.

items.heading: Static generation
items.text: Content and service pages: they load fast and reach search engines in full.

items.heading: Server-side rendering
items.text: Pages that change with the data but must appear complete on load.

items.heading: Client-side rendering
items.text: Interactive parts of a page that search engines don't need to read.

items.heading: Incremental regeneration
items.text: Regenerating pages when data changes, without a full redeploy.

items.question: When do I need Next.js instead of a ready-made platform?
items.answer: When you need an interactive interface, integrations with internal systems, or performance that ready-made platforms can't deliver with large volumes of data.

items.question: Does a Next.js website affect SEO?
items.answer: Not if the rendering method is chosen correctly. We use server-side rendering or static generation for pages that search engines need to read reliably.

items.question: Who manages the content?
items.answer: We connect the project to a separate CMS, so your team can edit text without touching the code.

items.question: Can it integrate with an existing system?
items.answer: Yes. We build the front end on top of your existing APIs, or develop new ones as needed.

items.question: How do you check performance?
items.answer: We measure load and interaction times in an environment close to production, and optimize images, bundles and the way data is fetched.

items.question: What about maintenance?
items.answer: We hand over documentation of the architecture, and we can agree on ongoing updates and continued development.
